chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Hammad ibn Isa, and Ibn Abi Umayr, and Ibn al-Mughira, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while we were in Medina: 'I have performed the Umrah of Rajab, and I intend to perform Hajj, so should I send the sacrificial animal (Hady) and perform Hajj al-Ifrad, or perform Hajj al-Tamattu?' He said: 'In each there is merit, and each is good.' I said: 'Which of them is superior?' He said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say that for every month, Umrat Tamattu' is superior, and by God, it is superior.' Then he said: 'Indeed, the people of Mecca say that his Umrah was Iraqi and his Hajj was Meccan, and they are lying. Is he not bound to his Hajj? He does not depart until he completes it.'

key_terms.حَجُّ التَّمَتُّعِ: Hajj al-Tamattu' (performing Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.حَجُّ الْإِفْرَادِ: Hajj al-Ifrad (performing Hajj alone, without Umrah)
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ رَجَبٍ: Umrah of the month of Rajab
key_terms.عُمْرَتُهُ عِرَاقِيَّةٌ: His Umrah was Iraqi (referring to Umrah al-Qada or Umrah al-Mufridah performed separately)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method of performing Hajj when combining it with Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the superiority of Umrat al-Tamattu' by citing the consistent practice of Imam Ali (AS), while refuting the Meccans' claim that the Prophet's Umrah and Hajj were distinct, unrelated events. He emphasizes the intrinsic connection between the two rites, noting that the Prophet did not depart until he completed his Hajj, thereby validating the Tamattu' mode as the most virtuous. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation of ritual practices over popular Meccan traditions.
